Test percentages against their counts with values around the reported ones

Source: R/percentage-of-map-seq.R
percentage_of_map_seq.Rd

percentage_of_map_seq() varies the reported counts, percentages, and totals a few steps up and down and applies percentage_of() to each resulting value set. This shows whether a small error in one of them could explain an inconsistency.

Call audit() on the output for summary statistics.

Usage

percentage_of_map_seq(
  data,
  digits_percentage,
  absolute = NULL,
  percentage = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  ...,
  rounding = "up_or_down",
  threshold = 5,
  symmetric = FALSE,
  var = c("absolute", "percentage", "n"),
  dispersion = 1:5,
  out_min = "auto",
  out_max = "auto",
  include_reported = FALSE,
  include_consistent = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame that percentage_of_map() could take.

digits_percentage

Integer. The number of decimal places in percentage, including trailing zeros. There is no default, since a numeric value does not keep them (1.40 is 1.4). Either a single number for the whole column or one number per row of data. If left out, it is taken from a digits_percentage column of data. It also sets the step size for dispersing percentage.

absolute, percentage, n

Optionally, the names of the columns in data that contain these values, if they differ from the defaults.

...

These dots must be empty. Every argument after them must be named in full.

rounding, threshold, symmetric

The same as in grim().

var

String. The variables to disperse. Default is c("absolute", "percentage", "n").

dispersion

Numeric. Steps up and down from the reported values, in units of the last decimal place. Default is 1:5.

out_min, out_max

Limits on the dispersed values. Both default to "auto", which keeps absolute and percentage at 0 or above and n at 1 or above. A number applies to every dispersed variable, and NULL removes the limit.

include_reported

Logical. Should the reported values themselves be part of the sequences? Default is FALSE.

include_consistent

Logical. Should consistent value sets be dispersed as well, not just inconsistent ones? Default is FALSE.

Value

A tibble with the columns of percentage_of_map() output plus diff_var, case, and var, as in grim_map_seq(). As there, the other columns of data are dropped.

Examples

df <- tibble::tibble(
  absolute = c(40, 37, 25),
  percentage = c(33, 31, 20),
  n = 120
)

df |>
  percentage_of_map_seq(digits_percentage = 0) |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 17
#>   absolute percentage     n consistency hits_total hits_absolute hits_percentage
#>      <int>      <dbl> <int> <lgl>            <int>         <int>           <int>
#> 1       25         20   120 FALSE                6             1               1
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: hits_n <int>, diff_absolute <int>,
#> #   diff_absolute_up <int>, diff_absolute_down <int>, diff_percentage <int>,
#> #   diff_percentage_up <int>, diff_percentage_down <int>, diff_n <int>,
#> #   diff_n_up <int>, diff_n_down <int>
